title: Germany – Consulting services for water-supply and waste consultancy – 10047131 - EPR Registry Development in Indonesia
description: Circular Economy (CE) with the focus on solid waste management is one of the key priorities of the Indonesian - German development cooperation. The project "InCircular: Promoting a Circular Economy in Indonesia" BMZ is supporting the Indonesian Ministry for National Development Planning (Bappenas) to implement the national Circular Economy Roadmap and Action Plan. Three material streams are of particular focus, namely packaging waste, electronic waste and residual waste to be used as refuse-derived fuel (RDF). InCircular pursues 5 Outputs (components): 1. Support the steering of the implementation of the CE Roadmap and Action Plan; 2. Enhance regulatory frameworks for CE and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for selected material streams; 3. Strengthen collaboration with industry for the implementation of CE and EPR for selected material streams; 4. Advance CE in waste management in selected provinces and municipalities; and 5. Advance Green/Sustainable Public Procurement for selected goods. This assignment is primarily anchored within Output 2. Indonesia generates approximately 70 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, of which an estimated 50-60% is mismanaged. Only 10-15% of plastic waste is recycled; the remainder is disposed of in uncontrolled landfills or leaks into the environment. Packaging waste is the most challenging stream. To date, no comprehensive legal framework for EPR has been established, but mandatory EPR for packaging is widely recognised by the GoI and the private sector as one central policy instrument to internalise the costs of packaging waste, mobilise private capital for collection and recycling infrastructure, and establish a level playing field across obligated producers. Indonesia has built a credible legal foundation on which EPR can be implemented. A new Presidential Decree on Waste Management (JAKSTRANAS) as well as a revised MoE Ministerial Regulation on the implementation of EPR are expected for late 2026. These would outline mandatory EPR for packaging and its modalities, marking a milestone in reforming waste management. These regulations will also form the foundation for this assignment to assist the establishment of a mandatory producer registry. A mandatory registry is important for establishing a level playing field among producers, calibrate the system based on good data, allow appropriate fee setting, estimate the infrastructure requirements and allow effective monitoring and enforcement of the regulations. The objective of this assignment is to develop a concept and strategy for the establishment of a professional, modern EPR Registry for Packaging, in line with international best practice and adjusted to the local context and latest regulatory developments in Indonesia, and to facilitate its implementation through guidance and capacity development. With this, it will contribute to supporting the Government of Indonesia in addressing packaging waste pollution through EPR. The assignment comprises the following work packages: Work package 1: EPR Registry Concept & Strategy Development This work package is the cornerstone of the contract. It encompasses a baseline analysis, the development of the concept and strategy for the EPR Registry in Indonesia. Work package 2: Capacity Development & Private Sector Consultations This work package comprises specific capacity development measures like trainings and workshops with public institutions on the development and implementation of the EPR registry concept as well as stakeholder consultations with the private sector in order to make the implementation of the system viable. Work package 3: (On Demand) Advisory Services for the Implementation of EPR This work package comprises more general, demand-based capacity development of the implementation of EPR in general.

title: 81322998-Development of a project pipeline for the CAFI Cameroon Partnership and related activities
description: As part of the overall PCIM project, the contractor will focus on 2 work packages - Work Package 1 (Output 2): Support to Cameroon"s National Research and Innovation System (SNRI) and coordination/harmonization of geographic data across ministries to provide coherent land-use and deforestation driver information. - Work Package 2 (Output 3): Preparation of the next CAFI-Cameroon phase via a project pipeline. Work Package 1 (Output 2) Activity 2.1.3: Support to a National Research and Innovation System (SNRI) - Purpose: Establish and develop a Cameroonian SNRI, supporting the National Strategy SND30, strengthen institutional conditions and the uptake of research and innovation. - Contractor tasks: close cooperation and coordination with the Ministry of Economy, Planning and Regional Development (MINEPAT) and the Ministry of Scientific Research and Innovation (MINRESI); Conduct a situational analysis/diagnosis of the SNRI; Develop an extended SNRI concept (actors, methods, processes, roles/mandates); Operationalize a permanent consultation framework (e.g., regulatory texts, documentation research); Identify innovative R&D projects (through calls for proposals/incubators) in concertation with GIZ and partners for subsequent financing; Develop an international research partnership strategy and organize a study trip for selected partners.; Develop a peatland conservation strategy. Activity 2.1.4: System for Digital and Satellite Mapping - Purpose: Support MINEPAT and sector ministries (e.g., Ministry of Agriculture MINADER, Ministry of Forests and Fauna MINFOF) and the National Observatory on Climate Change (ONACC) to produce and digitize real-time maps on forest cover/deforestation, forest resource use (mining/agriculture), and agro-sylvo-pastoral land; move toward a centralized, cross-ministerial system. - Contractor tasks: Map all actors currently producing cartographic material (beyond the National Institute of Cartography); Support the National Institute of Cartography in compiling, completing, and harmonizing cartographic datasets/parameters; Support MINFOF to improve SIGIF2 by: (i) operationalizing all modules incl. satellite imagery, (ii) establishing annual procedures to evaluate the traceability function, activating the national monitoring committee (APV FLEGT), and publishing evaluation and action plan on APV and MINFOF websites, (iii) interconnecting SIGIF2 with customs and tax systems and setting a roadmap to improve forestry taxation (MINFOF/MINFI); Support ONACC in climate monitoring reports (e.g., Forest Cover Loss Atlas 2000-2017; updated climate risk monitoring) to inform the National Adaptation Plan. Work Package 2 (Output 3) Activity 3.1.2: Feasibility Studies - Purpose: Provide robust decision bases for the project pipeline. - Deliverables: 15 Preliminary Economic Assessments (PEA), 15 pre-feasibility studies, 15 feasibility studies, plus capacity building for the Project Steering Unit (UGP). - Approach: Early expert involvement, stakeholder feedback (sector ministries and decentralized authorities), analysis of technical, economic, environmental, and climate aspects; results guide project design and management. Activity 3.1.3: Development of ProDocs - Based on portfolio design and studies: o Draft and submit ToR for Calls for Expressions of Interest (CEI) for implementing agencies to MINEPAT. o Coordinate validation of project outlines with UGP and CAFI Secretariat. o Note: MINEPAT selects/engages agencies; ProDocs and related workshops are produced by the selected agencies under MINEPAT supervision. o Provide technical support to agencies developing ProDocs; support MINEPAT in mobilizing finance (public/private, national/international, co financing, credit). o Target sectors: industry/energy, agro industry (priority crops, deforestation drivers), forest/wood, mines metallurgy steel (green mine), transport (market access in rural areas). Ensure alignment with NDS30, sector strategies, and deforestation free, climate compatible value chains. Activity 3.2.1: Study on Innovative Financing/Incentive Mechanisms - Analyze tools/models (project/results based finance, budget support, compensatory payments, benefit sharing, etc.), assess feasibility and viability. Activity 3.2.2: National Innovative Financing System - Develop and agree administrative procedures for simplified fund provision; produce a procedures manual for financial administration/management during tendering, selection, and awarding; define common concepts/standards for incentives/financing models; build capacities; apply within future projects/investment plans. Activity 3.2.3: Jurisdictional Eligibility for Sustainable Agro industry - Assess Cameroon"s compliance with financiers" jurisdictional criteria (e.g., &Green); consider EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). - Raise awareness among stakeholders (including agro industries; one day international conference); provide technical/financial support; develop capacity-building for the Project Steering Unit and stakeholders. Activity 3.2.4: Municipal Financing Mechanism for Ecological Performance (MFMPE) - Performance based payments from CAFI to regions/municipalities/land users aligned with land use/development; adapt CAFI information system; aim for national management via a dedicated unit in an accredited organization. - Contractor tasks: In depth analysis of institutional requirements in year 1; support setup and operations, incl. capacity building; Co develop institutional framework with FEICOM; Design and implement processes, procedures, and support documents (manual) subject to UGP/mandated organization approval; Support agreements between CAFI and the mandated organization for financial transfers/administration per national CAFI access procedures; Strengthen the Project Steering Unit and mandated organization capacities; Pilot the mechanism in one municipality; conduct annual independent financial audits; Support accreditation with CAFI Fund and GCF.

title: Modelling climate change impacts for coastal sites in West Africa
description: 2. Scope of Work and Key Tasks The outcomes of the models will be an integral part of the CREAF-project, informing management- and policy decisions at the local level, while also providing a framework for similar initiatives for other sites in the future. To achieve the most reliable predictions, models must be grounded in local conditions and consider the hydrodynamics, geomorphology, ecology and socio-economy of each site. The consultant(s) are therefore expected to work closely with local partners in collecting data and validating model results, as well as the interpretation and communication of model results. Specifically, the project shall focus on the following tasks: Key Tasks 1) Lead the development of climate change impact monitoring systems for key sites with different habitats and tidal characteristics, the Banc d"Arguin in Mauritania and the Bijagós Archipelago in Guinea Bissau. - Compile historical and projected climate data relevant to the selected sites. - Assist local partners in identifying available hydrodynamic, morphologic, environmental, socio-economic, and other relevant dataset, and/or developing suitable, cost-effective, field-based methodologies for long-term monitoring schemes for other parameters to model impacts. - Analyse local monitoring data, either from existing sources or from new field efforts. - Analyse remote sensing data that can be used to inform specific model parameters for which field observations are missing. - Consider the expansion to the Saloum Delta in Senegal. 2) Develop climate change impact models that best fit the local requirements. - Develop conceptual and mathematical representations of impact pathways. - Identify the most suitable combination of models for each site to predict ecosystem changes, and its implications for migratory birds and local communities, under different climate change scenarios. - Integrate GIS-based spatial analysis, where relevant. - Develop a minimum of 2 models, one for Banc d"Arguin and one for the Bijagós. - Ensure transparency, reproducibility, and scalability. - Consider suitability of models for the Saloum Delta (and explore necessary adjustments). 3) Model application - Calibrate the model using historical climate, morphological, ecological, and socio-economic data. - Run the model under multiple climate and socio-economic scenarios. - Validate results against observed trends or independent datasets. - Assess short-, medium-, and long-term risks to migratory birds and local communities. - Identify thresholds, and tipping points, and non-linear effects. - Map exposure of habitats, species groups and settlements to climate risk factors. - Generate outputs relevant to policy and management. 4) Model interpretation and use - Assist project partners in translating model outputs into actionable recommendations. - Support prioritisation of interventions. - Provide documentation for future model updates and use. The consultant/team of consultants is expected to have proven experience in developing climate change impact models for coastal (tidal) wetlands. This experience should be demonstrated through relevant projects, publications, or completed assignments, that include the integration of different climate change scenarios, hydrodynamic processes, and ecological responses, from both a theoretical and a practical perspective. Experience working with diverse stakeholder groups to develop policy and management recommendations based on model outputs, supported by examples of past stakeholder engagement or co-development processes, is highly desirable. Knowledge of the specific characteristics of the key sites, including the biophysical, ecological and socio-economic contexts, will be an advantage. For teams, clearly defined roles and responsibilities should be provided. The involvement of women and youth (18-35 years) is strongly encouraged and should be reflected in the proposed team composition. A close collaboration with partners from CWSS, the University of Groningen and experts from other project partner organisation is foreseen throughout the project and should be considered in the approach laid out in the tender. 3) Key deliverables - Inception Report with refined objectives, methodologies, scenarios, and data sources for selected sites. - Detailed guidelines for specific field methodologies to be implemented at the site level. - Climate, environmental & socio-economic data packages per site, including all data used for model parameterization. - At least two transparent, reproducible impact models (Banc d"Arguin and Bijagós), including GIS-based spatial components. - GIS-based maps of exposure of habitats, migratory bird groups, and local settlements to key climate risk factors. - Knowledge transfer: Translation of model outputs into actionable recommendations.
